title: Comparison Explorer 2.0
subtitle: A political-economic philosophy explorer — translation layer, not competing doctrine.
neutrality_rule: Present the strongest serious version of each philosophy before criticizing it. CC also lists assumptions, unknowns, and Stage 4 challenges.

layer1.title: Simple comparison
layer1.intro: Keep the first screen understandable. Click any cell for Why / Explain this.

capitalism.plain: Businesses are usually owned by private people or companies—not by the government.
capitalism.why: Private ownership lets people take risks, keep gains, and bear losses. The idea is that those closest to a business have the strongest reason to keep it productive.
capitalism.problem: How to motivate investment and careful use of productive resources without a central authority assigning every factory.
capitalism.incentives: Owners can gain if the business succeeds and lose if it fails—so they watch costs, quality, and customers.
capitalism.concentration: When ownership concentrates, markets can stop being competitive and political influence can rise with wealth.
capitalism.family_vs_monopoly: A family bakery and a monopoly utility are both 'private,' but they create very different power and household effects.
capitalism.socialism_says: Too much private ownership of key productive assets can concentrate wealth and workplace power.
capitalism.cc_says: Ownership should follow function, risk, and public purpose—not a single slogan. Private ownership is common; essential systems still face Ownership and Four Roles tests.

socialism.plain: More of the economy's productive assets are meant to be owned socially—by workers, communities, or the public—though forms vary widely.
socialism.why: Supporters argue private ownership of major capital lets a few people control livelihoods and surplus.
socialism.problem: What happens when ownership of productive capital concentrates wealth and power?
socialism.incentives: Social ownership aims to align production with social goals; critics ask who decides and how waste is disciplined.
socialism.concentration: Socialism often treats concentrated private capital as the core problem to redesign.
socialism.family_vs_monopoly: Many socialists distinguish small personal property from large productive capital.
socialism.socialism_says: This is the tradition's core answer.
socialism.cc_says: CC agrees concentrated ownership can become political power, but rejects treating public/social ownership as the default for every productive activity.

social-democracy.plain: Most businesses stay privately owned, while government taxes and regulates and provides major public services.
social-democracy.why: Keep market productivity while protecting people from insecurity and extreme inequality.
social-democracy.problem: Can markets stay productive without leaving households exposed?
social-democracy.incentives: Private ownership remains the main productive engine; politics redistributes and regulates around it.
social-democracy.concentration: Competition policy and welfare institutions try to blunt the worst effects of concentration.
social-democracy.family_vs_monopoly: Small business is welcomed; monopoly and essential services draw heavier public rules.
social-democracy.socialism_says: Often too accepting of private capital power.
social-democracy.cc_says: CC shares mixed-economy realism, then adds stricter ownership tests, Capture Loop discipline, and household-prosperity measurement.

communism.plain: In classical communist aims, productive capital is no longer privately owned; collective or state forms replace private appropriation.
communism.why: Eliminate class ownership of the means of production.
communism.problem: Class society built on private productive ownership.
communism.incentives: Theory emphasizes social production; practice often relied on planning targets and state authority.
communism.concentration: Private capital concentration is rejected; political concentration became a historical risk.
communism.family_vs_monopoly: Personal belongings differ from productive capital in Marxist distinctions.
communism.socialism_says: Communism is often framed as a further destination beyond socialism.
communism.cc_says: CC rejects abolishing private productive ownership as the path to prosperity and liberty.

cc.plain: Who should own something depends on what the thing does, who bears risk, what incentives matter, and whether a public claim is defensible.
cc.why: Ownership is a tool for prosperity and liberty—not a single ideology badge.
cc.problem: Preserve markets and initiative while preventing concentrated economic or political power from dominating citizens.
cc.incentives: Align ownership with risk and accountability; do not invent public claims without the waterfall.
cc.concentration: Extraction Test and Capture Loop watch when ownership becomes domination.
cc.family_vs_monopoly: Family business and monopoly fail different tests even if both are private.
cc.cc_says: This is the CC answer—see Ownership Spectrum in the unabridged Money Engine.

capitalism.plain: Prices mostly form through buying and selling—signals about scarcity and willingness to pay.
capitalism.why: Markets coordinate millions of decisions without one planner assigning every price.
capitalism.incentives: High prices attract supply; low prices discourage waste.
capitalism.concentration: Monopoly can set prices that are not competitive signals.
capitalism.family_vs_monopoly: Competitive prices discipline firms; monopoly prices may extract.
capitalism.socialism_says: Market prices can ignore social needs and unequal bargaining power.
capitalism.cc_says: Competitive markets are information systems; they need rules that keep them markets.

socialism.plain: Depending on the form, prices may be market-formed, planned, or mixed.
socialism.why: Prevent market outcomes from overriding social priorities.
socialism.problem: Market allocation can leave basic needs unmet.
socialism.incentives: Planning aims to direct resources; markets may still allocate consumer goods in some models.
socialism.concentration: Price power in private hands is a concern.
socialism.cc_says: CC prefers competitive price discovery, with public roles for clear public goods and market failures—not general price command.

social-democracy.plain: Markets set most prices; regulation and public provision reshape outcomes around health, education, and labor.
social-democracy.why: Keep price signals while correcting insecurity.
social-democracy.socialism_says: May leave too much to markets.
social-democracy.cc_says: Close neighbor on markets-plus-rules; CC emphasizes constitutional constraint and measurable household prosperity.

communism.plain: In classical planned forms, administrative targets and administered prices often replace market price discovery for major goods.
communism.incentives: Targets and quotas; information and shortage problems historically appeared.
communism.concentration: Planning authority concentrates economic decision power.
communism.socialism_says: Planning is a tool, not always identical to communism.
communism.cc_says: CC treats loss of competitive price signals as a major information risk.

cc.plain: Prices should generally emerge from competition. When they don't, ask why—and whether government should referee, provide, or own.
cc.why: Prices carry information no committee can fully invent.
cc.concentration: Non-competitive prices trigger Extraction and Role Conflict tests.
cc.family_vs_monopoly: Same cash-register activity can hide different market power.
cc.cc_says: See Money Engine competitive markets theory.

capitalism.plain: Government mainly protects property, contracts, and rights, and provides limited public goods—though real capitalist countries vary.
capitalism.problem: How to have order without central economic direction.
capitalism.concentration: Weak rules allow private power to become de facto government.
capitalism.family_vs_monopoly: Referee role fails if captured by monopolists.
capitalism.socialism_says: Too thin a state for social justice.
capitalism.cc_says: Agree on rights and rules; disagree that 'thin state' is enough when capture and essential systems matter.

socialism.plain: Government or social institutions take a larger role directing or owning parts of the economy.
socialism.why: Counter private capital power and secure social needs.
socialism.family_vs_monopoly: Public power may replace private monopoly—or become a new monopoly.
socialism.cc_says: CC allows public roles by function, constrained by Four Roles, Digital Due Process, and Capture Loop breakers.

social-democracy.plain: Government regulates markets and provides major services (health, education, insurance) while leaving most enterprise private.
social-democracy.problem: Insecurity and inequality under pure markets.
social-democracy.incentives: Taxes fund services; regulation sets floors.
social-democracy.concentration: Political contest over how large the state should be.
social-democracy.family_vs_monopoly: Services often universal; firms mostly private.
social-democracy.cc_says: Shares service and regulation logic; adds stricter COUNTABLE and Replacement Readiness discipline.

communism.plain: In historical communist states, government/party institutions often directed major economic activity.
communism.concentration: Economic and political authority fused—central CC warning.
communism.socialism_says: Not all socialists endorse that fusion.
communism.cc_says: Rejects fusing economic and political command in one authority.

cc.plain: Government is referee, provider of genuine public goods, occasional owner by function, and never a silent captured instrument of private power.
cc.family_vs_monopoly: Role Conflict Test when government wears too many hats.

capitalism.plain: After costs, remaining surplus generally belongs to owners—who may reinvest, save, or take profit.
capitalism.why: Reward risk and guide capital toward valued uses.
capitalism.problem: How to allocate surplus without a central plan.
capitalism.incentives: Profit attracts capital; losses repel it.
capitalism.concentration: Retained profits can compound ownership concentration.
capitalism.family_vs_monopoly: Competitive profit differs from monopoly rent.
capitalism.socialism_says: Workers create value that owners appropriate.
capitalism.cc_says: Surplus follows legitimate ownership and risk—but public claims require the waterfall, not slogans.

socialism.plain: More of productive surplus is meant to return to workers, communities, or the public.
socialism.why: Surplus should not permanently concentrate as private capital power.
socialism.incentives: Social return vs private return tradeoffs.
socialism.concentration: Aims to break capital concentration via surplus rules.
socialism.cc_says: Agrees surplus distribution shapes power; disagrees that socializing surplus is the default answer for every firm.

social-democracy.plain: Owners keep most profits; government taxes income and enterprise to fund public services.
social-democracy.why: Finance security without ending private enterprise.
social-democracy.concentration: Progressive taxation aims to blunt extremes.
social-democracy.family_vs_monopoly: Same tax logic applies unevenly in practice.
social-democracy.socialism_says: Leaves ownership of surplus largely private.
social-democracy.cc_says: Taxes are one public-income path; public enterprise claims still need waterfall discipline.

communism.plain: Private appropriation of productive profit is ultimately displaced.
communism.concentration: Surplus control shifts to political institutions.
communism.socialism_says: End-state relative to socialism in some theories.
communism.cc_says: Rejects abolishing private surplus claims as the prosperity path.

cc.plain: Surplus follows who owns, who invested, and who bore risk—then asks if competition, capture, and public financing create any defensible public claim.
cc.why: Honesty about incentives plus honesty about public claims.
cc.problem: Reward production without teleported public cash.
cc.family_vs_monopoly: Same sales can yield different ten-year ownership maps.

capitalism.plain: Success is often measured as growth, profits, innovation, and rising wealth—though societies add other goals.
capitalism.why: Expand what people can produce and consume.
capitalism.concentration: Aggregate growth can hide household stagnation.
capitalism.socialism_says: Growth without justice is not success.
capitalism.cc_says: Growth matters; household prosperity is the unit of success.

socialism.plain: Success emphasizes shared welfare, reduced class domination, and social provision.
socialism.incentives: Social metrics over private profit metrics.
socialism.cc_says: Shares household concern; measures via multi-dimensional prosperity, not only class categories.

social-democracy.plain: Success mixes productive growth with security—jobs, health, education, and floors against poverty.
social-democracy.family_vs_monopoly: Family security is a design goal.
social-democracy.socialism_says: May accept too much residual inequality.
social-democracy.cc_says: Neighbor goal; CC adds ownership, capture, and intergenerational capital tests.

communism.plain: Success is collective provision and classless social organization—in theory.
communism.cc_says: Rejects classless-abolition path; retains constitutional liberty constraints.

cc.plain: Success means households can earn, afford, own, secure time, and pass forward capability—without capture or fake COUNTABLE claims.
cc.why: People live in households, not GDP charts.
cc.concentration: Capture and extraction fail the success test.
cc.family_vs_monopoly: The Johnson Family illustration exists for this reason.
cc.cc_says: See Household Engine and Is/Is Not.

philosophies.name: Classical Liberalism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How can people live free under law while limiting arbitrary power?
philosophies.sixty_second: Classical liberalism emphasizes individual rights, limited government, rule of law, and often markets as voluntary coordination.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Enlightenment debates about rights, toleration, commerce, and constitutional government.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People are rights-bearing agents capable of judgment; power must be constrained.
philosophies.how_markets_work: Markets as extensions of voluntary exchange.
philosophies.what_government_does: Secure rights, enforce contracts, provide limited public goods.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Limited taxation for legitimate public functions.
philosophies.workers: Labor as free contract—historically contested in practice.
philosophies.inequality: Often accepts inequality from voluntary exchange; focuses on legal equality.
philosophies.poverty: Relief often private/charity plus limited public floors depending on thinker.
philosophies.monopoly: Suspicious of monopoly privilege granted by the state.
philosophies.political_power: Fear concentrated political power; later liberals also feared private domination.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Negative liberty and equal legal standing are central.
philosophies.success_looks_like: A free society under law with expanding commerce.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Freedom under impersonal rules beats personal domination.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Can underweight economic power as a liberty threat; historical exclusions.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Real liberal societies mixed slavery, empire, suffrage limits, and later welfare states.

WE_AGREE_HERE: Rights, constitutional constraint, suspicion of arbitrary power
WE_DISAGREE_HERE: That thin government alone guarantees household prosperity
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Extend liberty analysis to capture and economic domination
WE_REJECT_THIS: Any claim that markets need no constitutional discipline

philosophies.variants_note: Includes Lockean, Smithian, and later constitutional strands—not one manifesto.

depths.plain: Classical liberalism emphasizes individual rights, limited government, rule of law, and often markets as voluntary coordination.
depths.deep: Real liberal societies mixed slavery, empire, suffrage limits, and later welfare states.
depths.technical: Technical distinctions and source trails deepen in later Explorer passes; unabridged remains source of truth.

philosophies.name: Laissez-Faire Capitalism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How do we coordinate production with minimal political interference?
philosophies.sixty_second: Laissez-faire capitalism favors private ownership and market allocation with a very limited state—mainly rights, contracts, and basic order.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Classical political economy reacting against mercantilist privilege.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People respond to incentives; interference often creates privilege.
philosophies.how_markets_work: Prices and competition should run with minimal intervention.
philosophies.what_government_does: Night-watchman functions; hostility to industrial policy and heavy redistribution.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Low, simple taxes in ideal form.
philosophies.inequality: Inequality often treated as acceptable outcome of freedom.
philosophies.poverty: Primarily private responsibility; public relief debated.
philosophies.monopoly: Opposes state-backed monopoly; pure theory trusts competition.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Economic liberty is central to liberty.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Strongest case: markets discover information politics cannot.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Underestimates market power, externalities, and capture; can romanticize 'free' markets that were never free of power.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: No large society ran textbook laissez-faire for long; infrastructure, money, and war always involved states.

WE_DISAGREE_HERE: That minimal state is sufficient against capture and essential-system failures
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Add constitutional tests for competition, public goods, and household outcomes
WE_REJECT_THIS: Automatic identification of deregulation with liberty

philosophies.variants_note: This tradition contains substantial internal variation. Treat this page as a fair map, not a single fixed doctrine.

philosophies.name: Modern Market Capitalism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How do corporations, finance, and global markets organize production today?
philosophies.sixty_second: Modern market capitalism is the mixed reality of private enterprise, corporate forms, finance, regulation, and global trade—not a pure theory.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Industrial and corporate evolution from the 19th–21st centuries.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People act through firms, jobs, credit, and households inside institutions.
philosophies.who_owns_productive_property: Mostly private, often through corporations and funds.
philosophies.who_controls_capital: Managers, boards, and financial markets allocate much capital.
philosophies.what_government_does: Regulate, stabilize, tax, and sometimes industrial-policy nudge.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Income, payroll, corporate, sales, and other taxes in practice.
philosophies.what_happens_to_profits: Owners/shareholders claim residual; taxes claim a share.
philosophies.workers: Employment relation; unions and labor law vary.
philosophies.poverty: Mix of markets, charity, and public programs.
philosophies.monopoly: Antitrust exists unevenly; scale often celebrated.
philosophies.political_power: Lobbying and campaign finance link wealth to rules.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Formal liberties with unequal economic power.
philosophies.success_looks_like: Growth, profits, asset values—plus political goals layered on.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Enormous productivity and consumer abundance are real.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Concentration, fragility, and household insecurity are also real.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Always a hybrid; 'capitalism' in speech often means this messy mixture.

WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Treating status quo corporate power as natural law
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Discipline with Extraction Test, Capture Loop, household metrics

philosophies.name: Social Democracy
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: Can we keep market productivity while protecting people from insecurity and extreme inequality?
philosophies.sixty_second: Social democracy keeps mostly private enterprise and markets, then uses taxation, regulation, and public services to provide security and opportunity.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Labor movements and reformist socialism in industrial democracies; Nordic and European postwar models as touchstones (not copies).
philosophies.believes_about_people: People need both freedom to produce and protection from market shocks.
philosophies.how_markets_work: Markets plus labor and product regulation.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Significant taxation of income and consumption.
philosophies.what_happens_to_profits: Private profits with tax-funded social wage.
philosophies.workers: Stronger labor rights and collective bargaining in many variants.
philosophies.inequality: Compress via taxes and services; not abolish classes.
philosophies.poverty: Universal or broad social insurance approaches.
philosophies.political_power: Democratic politics as the allocator of social claims.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Positive and negative liberties combined in practice.
philosophies.success_looks_like: High living standards with security floors.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Historically delivered broad middle-class security in several countries.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Fiscal pressure, insider/outsider labor divides, and globalization constraints.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Not 'socialism' in the public-ownership sense; hybrids differ by country.

WE_AGREE_HERE: Markets plus security; democratic legitimacy of social insurance
WE_DISAGREE_HERE: That tax-and-transfer alone solves ownership and capture problems
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Add ownership spectrum, COUNTABLE firewall, Replacement Readiness
WE_REJECT_THIS: Equating CC with any one Nordic fiscal package

philosophies.name: Democratic Socialism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How can democratic politics extend into ownership and economic power without dictatorship?
philosophies.sixty_second: Democratic socialism seeks deeper social ownership or control of capital through democratic means—beyond social-democratic compromise.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Socialist movements distinguishing themselves from authoritarian communism.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People should democratically shape economic life, not only elections.
philosophies.how_markets_work: Markets may remain in sectors; contested.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Taxes plus public enterprise returns in many programs.
philosophies.workers: Workplace democracy and labor power emphasized.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Expand democratic freedom; critics fear economic coercion.
philosophies.success_looks_like: Democratic control of investment and essentials.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Takes seriously that political equality can be hollow under extreme capital inequality.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Ambiguity about which sectors to socialize; investment and innovation risks; coalition difficulty.

WE_MODIFY_THIS: Channel into Role Conflict, ownership-by-function, and rights floors
WE_REJECT_THIS: Any path that weakens constitutional rights to win economic goals

depths.deep: Label covers many incompatible programs.

philosophies.name: Socialism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: What happens when ownership of productive capital concentrates wealth and power?
philosophies.sixty_second: Socialism, in broad form, seeks to socialize or democratize ownership and control of productive capital to varying degrees.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Industrial-era critique of capital concentration and wage labor.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People are social producers; private capital can dominate life chances.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Public claims on surplus; tax forms vary.
philosophies.workers: Empower workers as a class or as co-owners.
philosophies.monopoly: Replace private monopoly with social forms.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Freedom from capital domination; debates on political liberty.
philosophies.success_looks_like: Shared welfare and reduced class domination.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Names a real problem: capital concentration can become domination.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Information, incentive, and political-concentration failure modes in practice.

WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Social ownership as the general answer
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Translate into Extraction Test and Capture Loop without default socialization

depths.deep: Umbrella term—always specify the variant.

philosophies.name: Communism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How to end class society based on private ownership of the means of production?
philosophies.sixty_second: Communism aims at a classless society without private productive ownership; historical states that claimed the name often fused party and economic power.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Marxist and related traditions; 20th-century state experiments.
philosophies.believes_about_people: Humans can organize production without capitalist class relations.
philosophies.who_owns_productive_property: Collective/state forms ultimately displace private productive ownership.
philosophies.what_government_does: Directs or becomes the economy in historical cases.
philosophies.workers: Workers as associated producers in theory.
philosophies.political_power: In theory, politics transforms; in practice, party-state power concentrated.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Emancipation claim; historical rights record often catastrophic.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Industrial mobilization achieved certain production goals in some periods.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Shortages, repression, and information failures; ordinary households often paid the price.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Never confuse theory, slogan, and historical regime.

WE_AGREE_HERE: Warning that economic and political power can fuse
WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Abolition of private productive ownership as prosperity path
WE_BORROW_THIS: Attention to class structure of ownership
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Use as negative lesson for Capture and planning information problems
WE_REJECT_THIS: Party-state fusion; rights subordinated to plan

philosophies.name: State Capitalism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: What if the state owns or directs capital while markets and wage labor continue?
philosophies.sixty_second: State capitalism describes systems where the state is a major owner or controller of capital while market exchange and wage labor persist.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Used analytically for various 20th–21st century cases; contested label.
philosophies.what_happens_to_profits: State as residual claimant in key sectors.
philosophies.inequality: Depends on regime; can be severe.
philosophies.poverty: May use subsidies and public employment.
philosophies.political_power: Political control of economic commanding heights.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Often weak political liberty even with growth.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Can build infrastructure and export capacity quickly.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Role conflict, soft budgets, and political repression risks.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Not identical to socialism or to Western mixed economies.

WE_AGREE_HERE: State can own without ending markets
WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Blurring referee and owner without Role Conflict Test
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Force through Four Roles and Digital Due Process
WE_REJECT_THIS: Growth without constitutional liberty as success

philosophies.name: Mercantilism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How can a state grow power and treasure in a competitive international system?
philosophies.sixty_second: Mercantilism treated trade, bullion, and privileged companies as instruments of state power.
philosophies.who_owns_productive_property: Privileged companies and chartered monopolies common.
philosophies.how_markets_work: Managed trade; not free trade ideal.
philosophies.what_happens_to_profits: Privileged profits tied to state goals.
philosophies.workers: Labor subordinated to national power projects.
philosophies.monopoly: Monopoly privileges granted by the crown.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: State capacity and strategic trade awareness.

WE_AGREE_HERE: Strategic awareness that trade policy is power-laden
WE_BORROW_THIS: Attention to external income and national capacity
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Replace privilege with competitive capability rules

philosophies.name: Libertarianism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How far can voluntary exchange and private property replace political authority?
philosophies.sixty_second: Libertarianism maximizes individual liberty and private property, minimizing coercive state functions—sometimes to anarcho-capitalist extremes.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Modern revival of classical liberal themes with sharper anti-state edge.
philosophies.believes_about_people: Adults as self-owners; consent is the moral core.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Voluntary funding ideals; oppose most taxation.
philosophies.monopoly: Against state monopoly; debates on private monopoly.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Sharp critique of coercion and bureaucratic overreach.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Public goods, externalities, and private power undertreated; historical dependence on public order.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Wide spectrum from minarchist to anarcho-capitalist.

WE_DISAGREE_HERE: That markets alone dissolve the need for constitutional public authority
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Keep rights floors while retaining legitimate public roles
WE_REJECT_THIS: Abolition of public authority over essential systems by slogan

depths.plain: Libertarianism maximizes individual liberty and private property, minimizing coercive state functions—sometimes to anarcho-capitalist extremes.
depths.deep: Wide spectrum from minarchist to anarcho-capitalist.

philosophies.name: Conservatism / Fusionist Economic Tradition
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How to preserve order, tradition, and liberty while accepting markets?
philosophies.sixty_second: American fusionism joined social conservatism with market economics and anti-statism—an alliance, not a single economic science.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People need moral order and free enterprise.
philosophies.who_controls_capital: Private capital with skepticism of planning.
philosophies.what_government_does: Limited economic state; stronger moral/cultural ambitions vary.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Lower taxes favored in many programs.
philosophies.workers: Ambivalent: pro-business and pro-family wage ideals coexist.
philosophies.inequality: Often secondary to growth and order.
philosophies.political_power: Distrust of concentrated left political power; softer on business power historically.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Not identical to classical liberalism or populism.

WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Treating business power as automatically virtuous
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Apply Capture Loop evenly to economic allies
WE_REJECT_THIS: Nostalgia as a substitute for measurement

philosophies.name: Progressive Political Economy
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How should democratic government discipline concentrated private power and expand security?
philosophies.sixty_second: Progressive political economy uses regulation, taxation, public investment, and rights expansions to curb private domination and broaden opportunity.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Progressive Era through New Deal and later U.S. reform traditions.
philosophies.believes_about_people: Citizens need protection from both market and corporate coercion.
philosophies.who_controls_capital: Public steering of investment in key eras.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Antitrust and social insurance answered real Gilded Age harms.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Bureaucracy, capture of regulators, and exclusion errors in program design.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Progressivism is a family, not one statute.

WE_AGREE_HERE: Antitrust; public investment can expand household wealth
WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Assuming more agencies automatically equal more justice
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Add Replacement Readiness and COUNTABLE honesty

philosophies.name: Distributism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How can property be widespread enough that families are not proletarianized?
philosophies.sixty_second: Distributism seeks widely distributed productive property—many owners—rather than concentration in either capitalists or the state.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Early 20th-century Catholic social thought (Chesterton/Belloc lineage) and related currents.
philosophies.believes_about_people: Families flourish with real productive stakes.
philosophies.what_government_does: Break up concentrations; foster ownership breadth.
philosophies.workers: Prefer owner-workers to pure wage dependence.
philosophies.inequality: Inequality of property is the issue.
philosophies.monopoly: Against both monopoly capital and monopoly state.
philosophies.political_power: Suspicious of concentrated power either side.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Scale, technology, and capital intensity challenges.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Not a full modern macro program.

WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Romantic smallness as universal industrial form
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Connect to Ownership Spectrum and cooperatives without anti-scale dogma

philosophies.name: Georgism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How to socialize land rents without destroying productive enterprise?
philosophies.sixty_second: Georgism distinguishes land/natural opportunity from produced capital, proposing to socialize land rent while leaving labor and capital products private.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Henry George and land-value tax traditions.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People create value; land rents are different.
philosophies.who_owns_productive_property: Private improvements; social claim on land value.
philosophies.how_markets_work: Markets for goods; land rent redirected.
philosophies.what_government_does: Collect land rent; otherwise limited in pure form.
philosophies.what_happens_to_profits: Produced profits remain private; land rent socialized.
philosophies.monopoly: Less focused on industrial monopoly than land monopoly.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Liberty of production with socialized rent.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Cleanly separates land rent from productive effort.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Assessment, transition, and political economy of landowners.

WE_DISAGREE_HERE: Single-tax as sufficient fiscal system for Arkansas

philosophies.name: Constitutional Capitalism
philosophies.problem_it_tries_to_solve: How do we preserve decentralized markets, private initiative, ownership and liberty while preventing either concentrated economic power or concentrated government power from dominating citizens—and make prosperity compound across households, communities and generations?
philosophies.sixty_second: Constitutional Capitalism is a political-economic architecture: competitive markets and broadening ownership under constitutional constraint, democratic accountability, and public-purpose discipline—with household prosperity as the unit of success.
philosophies.where_it_came_from: Integration of constitutional government, market discovery, ownership-by-function, capture discipline, and intergenerational capital—see Unabridged Parts I–VII.
philosophies.believes_about_people: People are rights-bearing household members who need capability, ownership paths, and freedom from domination.
philosophies.who_owns_productive_property: Depends on function, risk, incentives, and public purpose—not a single slogan.
philosophies.who_controls_capital: Private initiative primary; public claims only after waterfall.
philosophies.how_markets_work: Competitive markets as information systems that need rules to remain markets.
philosophies.what_government_does: Four roles under popular sovereignty; Digital Due Process; Capture Loop breakers.
philosophies.how_government_raises_money: Taxes and legitimate public returns—never teleported COUNTABLE cash.
philosophies.what_happens_to_profits: Follows ownership/risk; public share only when defensible.
philosophies.workers: Capability, compensation, and ownership pathways—not only jobs.
philosophies.inequality: Problem when it becomes capture; not automatically solved by growth.
philosophies.poverty: Capability and security without fake fiscal promises.
philosophies.monopoly: Extraction Test; competition policy; ownership alternatives.
philosophies.individual_liberty: Constitutional rights floors; no trade of rights for economic slogans.
philosophies.why_supporters_believe: Joins market discovery with anti-capture constitutionalism and honest measurement.
philosophies.what_critics_say: Unproven fiscal engines; legal constraints; implementation capacity; Stage 4 attack surface.
philosophies.where_reality_gets_complicated: Not a finished country—an attackable blueprint. Stage 3 certified completeness to test, not truth of every hypothesis.

WE_AGREE_HERE: Markets need rules; ownership shapes power; households are the unit of success
WE_DISAGREE_HERE: N/A — this is the home page of the architecture
WE_BORROW_THIS: Market discovery; constitutional rights; social insurance insights; ownership breadth; public investment lessons
WE_MODIFY_THIS: Join them under Dependency Rule, waterfall, and household metrics
WE_REJECT_THIS: Laissez-faire purity; socialism-as-default; growth-alone; fake COUNTABLE

concepts.title: Ownership
concepts.question: Who should own things?
storytelling_spine: What happens to our example household

depths.plain: Ownership means who has the right to control an asset, bear its risks, and claim what it produces after obligations.
depths.deep: Ownership is a bundle: control, residual claim, alienation, and liability. Political economies disagree on which productive assets should be private, cooperative, or public.
depths.technical: See Ownership Spectrum and Extraction Test in the Money Engine; beneficial ownership differs from legal title.

concepts.imagine_this: Two neighbors run food businesses. One owns the kitchen equipment and the building. The other rents everything and keeps only wages. Same customers—different futures.

cases.problem: Scale industries, finance, and weak competition rules
cases.changed: Corporate consolidation in rail, oil, steel, banking
cases.owned: Private trusts and financiers concentrated control
cases.markets: National markets expanding; competition often crushed
cases.government: Later Progressive antitrust and regulation responses
cases.households: Rising urban employment with harsh conditions for many
cases.failed: Competitive markets and equal political voice under strain

cases.not_a_transplant: Arkansas is not 1890 New York finance.

cases.title: United States — New Deal / Postwar Era
cases.tagline: Private business + public institutions building a middle class—unevenly
cases.question: Can public institutions expand private household wealth—and who gets included?
cases.changed: Social Security, labor law, infrastructure, mortgage and education policies
cases.households: Broad middle-class gains for many; exclusions in some programs
cases.failed: Racial and regional exclusions; later stagflation debates
cases.later: Neoliberal reforms and new inequality patterns
cases.arkansas_lesson: Public institutions can expand household wealth; design who is included.
cases.not_a_transplant: Copying 1950 federal packages wholesale is not the method.

cases.title: Tennessee Valley Authority
cases.tagline: Public ownership of infrastructure for regional capability
cases.question: When might government own productive infrastructure?
cases.before: Poverty, floods, limited electrification in the Valley
cases.problem: Private incentives weak for regional transformation at that scale
cases.financed: Federal capitalization and rate revenues over time
cases.households: Electrification transformed domestic and farm life
cases.failed: Displacement, environmental, and governance costs contested
cases.arkansas_lesson: Public ownership isn't automatically good or bad—apply Ownership and Four Roles tests.
cases.not_a_transplant: TVA is a historical instrument, not a blank check.

cases.title: Rural Electrification
cases.tagline: Cooperatives where private utilities would not wire the countryside
cases.question: What institutional form fits a thin-density network problem?
cases.problem: Low density made private wiring uneconomic
cases.failed: Not a template for providing everything publicly
cases.later: Ongoing co-op governance and broadband analogies
cases.arkansas_lesson: Different problems need different structures—especially relevant for Arkansas.
cases.not_a_transplant: Co-ops ≠ government should run every sector.

cases.title: Norway — Resource Wealth Institutions
cases.tagline: Markets + private enterprise + public resource claim + sovereign investment
cases.question: How can resource rents become intergenerational capital?
cases.problem: Oil windfall risk of temporary binge
cases.changed: Public resource framework + large investment fund
cases.owned: Public claim on petroleum rents; private enterprise elsewhere
cases.financed: Resource rents invested, not only spent
cases.households: High living standards with oil-funded public capacity
cases.later: Ongoing fund rules and political debate
cases.arkansas_lesson: Design principle for rents and intergenerational capital—not copy Norway.
cases.not_a_transplant: Different resources, population, constitution, history, fiscal position.

cases.title: Singapore
cases.tagline: Intense capability-building with major state involvement and global markets
cases.question: What happens when government focuses intensely on productive capacity?
cases.changed: State-linked enterprises, housing, compulsory savings, open trade
cases.owned: Mix of private and state-linked capital
cases.households: Rapid material gains; political structure distinct
cases.failed: Economic effectiveness ≠ automatic validation of political structure
cases.arkansas_lesson: Capability focus matters; Constitutional comes before Capitalism for a reason.
cases.not_a_transplant: City-state politics and scale are not Arkansas.

cases.title: Germany — Social Market Economy
cases.tagline: Competitive markets protected as a constitutional economic order
cases.question: Can the state protect the conditions necessary for competitive markets?
cases.problem: Rebuild without laissez-faire myth or central planning
cases.changed: Ordoliberal/social-market institutions, competition policy, social protections
cases.owned: Private property with social obligations themes
cases.failed: Not identical to CC; European institutional specifics
cases.arkansas_lesson: Markets need rules that keep them markets.
cases.not_a_transplant: CC is not simply American ordoliberalism.

cases.title: Mondragón
cases.tagline: A large cooperative network made ownership concrete
cases.question: How does worker ownership work at scale?
cases.financed: Internal capital and cooperative banking traditions
cases.households: Member livelihoods tied to co-op health
cases.failed: Capital constraints; crisis governance hard cases
cases.arkansas_lesson: Compare corporation ↔ ESOP ↔ cooperative ↔ public enterprise concretely.

cases.title: Soviet Union
cases.tagline: Central planning and fused political-economic power
cases.question: What happens when economic and political decision-making concentrate in the same authority?
cases.households: Security of some goods; shortages and repression costs
cases.arkansas_lesson: Power and economics are one problem.
cases.not_a_transplant: Not a cartoon of all left ideas—a specific historical system.

cases.title: China — Mao era to Reform era
cases.tagline: From collectivized planning toward markets under continued state power
cases.question: Can markets operate without liberal democratic government?
cases.problem: Growth and modernization under CCP authority
cases.changed: Market mechanisms, private enterprise, FDI, state direction retained
cases.government: Authoritarian political structure with developmental state features
cases.households: Massive material gains for many; political constraints
cases.worked: Growth via markets under state power
cases.arkansas_lesson: Why the word Constitutional comes first.
cases.not_a_transplant: Political system not a model for Arkansas.

cases.title: Venezuela — Oil dependence caution
cases.tagline: Public promises on a volatile commodity base
cases.question: What happens when public promises depend heavily on one volatile income source?
cases.problem: Fiscal and political dependence on petroleum
cases.changed: Heavy state ownership/intervention, price controls, institutional deterioration
cases.households: Collapse in living standards for many
cases.arkansas_lesson: Why we refuse to count hypothetical public revenue; resilience rules matter.
cases.not_a_transplant: Do not teach 'socialism = Venezuela.' Teach mechanisms.

cases.title: Japan & South Korea — Developmental capitalism
cases.question: Can a country deliberately build productive capability without replacing markets?
cases.changed: Education, finance, export discipline, industrial policy variants
cases.households: Rapid income gains; later demographic stress
cases.failed: Bubbles, demographics, corporate governance issues differ by country
cases.arkansas_lesson: Capability strategy is real; still needs constitutional and household tests.
cases.not_a_transplant: Cold War geopolitics and scale differ.

cases.title: Estonia — Digital government
cases.question: What becomes possible—and what safeguards become necessary?
cases.owned: Market economy with digital public rails
cases.failed: Privacy/security must be designed, not assumed

cases.title: Alaska Permanent Fund
cases.tagline: Resource wealth → public asset → citizen dividend
cases.question: What is the difference between a dividend and productive public financing?
cases.problem: Share resource rents with citizens over time
cases.worked: Visible citizen claim on resource wealth
cases.failed: Dividend ≠ full fiscal system; politics of withdrawals
cases.arkansas_lesson: Principle of public asset from rents—not copy-paste oil dividend.
cases.not_a_transplant: Arkansas lacks Alaska's exact resource structure.

cases.title: Arkansas — Scale economics (Walmart lens)
cases.tagline: Follow money, ownership, competition, household and community effects
cases.question: What does enormous scale do to prices, suppliers, labor, and local retail?
cases.problem: Logistics and price competition at continental scale
cases.owned: Publicly traded corporation with Arkansas roots
cases.markets: Intense price competition; supplier power shifts
cases.government: Ordinary corporate and labor law environment
cases.households: Lower prices for consumers; labor and local merchant effects contested
cases.worked: Logistics productivity and consumer price effects
cases.failed: No predetermined moral verdict—run the analytical method
cases.later: Ongoing labor, community, and antitrust debates
cases.arkansas_lesson: Use CC method: money, ownership, competition, household, community—without a cartoon villain/hero script.
cases.not_a_transplant: One firm is not an economic system.

answers.answer: If demand cannot support it economically, resources may need to move elsewhere.
Public subsidy may preserve access as part of universal social provision.
Healthcare provision may be publicly/socially owned as a basic service.

First establish the necessary public function; then test market viability, externalities, household effects, ownership alternatives, regional capacity, public role, cost, resilience, and measurable outcome.

items.title: A corporation controls 80% of an essential market

answers.answer: Prefer entry and innovation; distrust political fixes that create new privilege.
Break up or regulate as countervailing public power.
Socialize or heavily democratize the essential sector.
Run Extraction Test, competition remedies, Role Conflict Test, and household effect—choose the least-dominating effective tool.

items.question: Arkansas has $1 billion. What should we do with it?

voices.reasoning: Prefer returning resources to private investment and households unless a clear public good fails privately.
Invest in universal services and human capital that markets under-provide.
Build productive capability and infrastructure that compounds.
Map to household prosperity and public-goods tests; no COUNTABLE fantasy; measure outcomes; avoid capture.

history_warning_lights.title: Monopoly concentration
history_warning_lights.lesson: Successful firms can cease to be competitive markets.

ux_rule: Never ask the reader to understand the vocabulary before they understand the idea.
